title: Pure substances & mixtures
examples: What is the difference between a compound and a mixture?
How can I tell if a substance is pure?
Can you give an example of a natural mixture?

explain.say: Today we will learn about different types of matter.
An element is a pure substance made of only one type of atom.
A compound is a pure substance made when two or more elements chemically combine.
A mixture combines two or more substances that are not chemically joined together.
We can check purity by looking at the melting point of a substance.
Consider saltwater, which is a mixture of salt and water.

faq.q: How do I know if something is a compound or a mixture?
faq.a: Compounds have a fixed ratio of elements chemically bonded together. Mixtures can have any ratio and are just mixed together physically.
asks: What is the difference between chemical and physical combination?
Can you tell me if something is bonded or just mixed?

faq.q: What does a sharp melting point tell me?
faq.a: A sharp melting point indicates that the substance is pure. This means it is made of only one type of substance.
asks: If the melting point changes, what does that mean?
Is a changing melting point a sign of impurity?

faq.a: Yes, an element is by definition a pure substance because it consists of only one type of atom.
asks: Does having only one element mean it is pure?

faq.q: Can a compound melt over a range of temperatures?
faq.a: No, a pure compound will melt sharply at a specific temperature. A range of melting points suggests it is a mixture.
asks: If it melts slowly, is it impure?
Does the melting point tell us if it's a compound?

faq.q: What is the simplest example of a mixture?
faq.a: A simple example is sand and gravel mixed together. They are physically mixed and can be separated easily.
asks: Can I separate a mixture using simple methods?

facts: Elements are the simplest pure substances.
Compounds always form in a fixed ratio.
Mixtures can be separated by physical means.
Pure substances have a distinct melting point.

quiz.say: Which substance has a sharp, fixed melting point?
quiz.show: A pure substance has a sharp melting point.
quiz.why: Compounds are pure substances formed by chemical bonds, so they melt sharply.

wrong.1: Mixtures melt over a range of temperatures because they are not chemically bonded.
wrong.2: While elements are pure, the question asks generally about the characteristic shown by melting point, which applies to both pure compounds and elements.
wrong.3: A solution is a type of mixture and will show a range of melting points.

quiz.say: If I mix iron filings and sulfur powder, what have I created?
quiz.why: Mixing substances physically without a chemical reaction creates a mixture.

wrong.0: A compound requires a chemical reaction to form, which is not happening when you just mix them.
wrong.1: The resulting combination is not pure because it contains two different components.
wrong.3: Iron and sulfur are elements, but mixing them does not make the resulting substance an element.

quiz.say: Water (H2O) is classified as which type of matter?
quiz.why: Water is formed when hydrogen and oxygen chemically combine in a fixed ratio.

wrong.0: Water contains two different types of atoms, hydrogen and oxygen, so it cannot be an element.
wrong.1: Because the atoms are chemically bonded, it is not merely a physical mix like salt water.
wrong.2: This term is too general; water is specifically a compound.
